what: Keurig Dr Pepper sells drinks in North America. It owns Dr Pepper, 7UP, Snapple, Canada Dry and Mott's, the Keurig single-serve coffee system and the pods that go in it, and the energy brand Ghost.
customers: Supermarkets, convenience stores, restaurants and households buying coffee pods and brewers.
money: Dr Pepper, Canada Dry, 7UP and energy drinks
moat: Brands people ask for by name, plus the Keurig installed base: each brewer sold creates years of pod sales.
risks: Debt of about $26 billion is high relative to earnings
Coffee pod volumes have been declining as at-home coffee demand normalised
Green coffee prices rose sharply, squeezing the coffee margin
Plans to split the company have created uncertainty
opportunities: Dr Pepper has been taking share and is now a top-two US soft drink brand
Energy drinks through Ghost and distribution deals grow faster than soft drinks
watch: Coffee segment volumes and margins, and Dr Pepper market share.
